items.title: Senior Enterprise Product Manager, FP&A
items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” Learn more about working at Coinbase . The Enterprise Applications and Architecture (EAA) team builds the internal platforms, systems, and workflows that help Coinbase operate effectively at scale. Within that space, this Product Manager role will focus on FP&A and adjacent finance workflows, with ownership across planning, forecasting, reporting, workflow automation, and the systems experience that finance teams rely on day to day. This is a high-ownership L5 PM role for a leader who can bring structure to a broad problem space and partner effectively across Finance, Engineering, Business Systems, Data, and Functional Architecture. The scope spans core planning workflows like budgeting, forecasting, headcount management, and close-adjacent processes, along with reporting, variance analysis, executive visibility, and platform-level improvements that make FP&A tooling more scalable, reliable, and AI-enabled over time. What you’ll be doing (ie. job duties): Own product strategy, roadmap, and execution for FP&A product surfaces and workflows across planning, reporting, and automation. Partner closely with Finance and EAA leadership to define the future-state FP&A operating model and the product investments required to support it. Drive improvements to budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, and finance operating rhythms through better systems, workflows, and user experiences. Improve reporting and insight delivery for finance and business leaders by shaping dashboards, variance analysis experiences, and decision-support tooling. Lead platform-level product work that improves the scalability, maintainability, and interoperability of FP&A systems and workflows. Identify and prioritize opportunities to use AI and workflow automation to reduce manual effort, improve data quality, and shorten planning and reporting cycles. Translate ambiguous stakeholder needs into clear requirements, measurable outcomes, and sequenced delivery plans. Operate as the product DRI across multiple teams, ensuring alignment on priorities, tradeoffs, timing, and business impact. Define success metrics and use quantitative and qualitative signals to continuously improve outcomes for Finance users. What we look for in you (ie. job requirements): 5+ years of Product Management experience, including ownership of complex internal platforms, enterprise software, or workflow-heavy products. Strong product judgment in cross-functional environments with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and high expectations for execution. Experience working on finance systems, planning platforms, enterprise workflows, or adjacent domains where process rigor and data quality matter. Ability to deeply understand user pain points across both operational workflows and executive reporting use cases. Strong analytical orientation with the ability to define metrics, evaluate tradeoffs, and use data to inform roadmap decisions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders and align technical and non-technical partners. Demonstrated ability to move ambiguous problem spaces toward clear product strategy and execution. Demonstrates the ability to responsibly use generative AI tools and copilots in daily workflows, continuously learn as tools evolve, and apply human-in-the-loop practices to deliver business-ready outputs and measurable improvements in efficiency, quality, and cost. Demonstrated AI and workflow automation fluency, especially in environments where automation can materially improve finance operations. Nice to haves: Experience supporting FP&A, Finance, or business operations teams with internal product or systems work. Familiarity with planning, forecasting, reporting, enterprise performance management, or close-adjacent finance workflows. Experience with data and analytics products, including dashboarding and KPI instrumentation. Experience partnering with enterprise architecture, business systems, or platform engineering teams. Familiarity with fintech, regulated environments, or high-growth technology companies. Curiosity about crypto and willingness to ramp quickly on Coinbase products and business context. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. The Consumer team owns the Kraken app experience used by millions of traders and crypto newcomers worldwide, the product that turns someone's first crypto curiosity into a long-term relationship with Kraken. We build the interfaces people actually use to buy, sell, manage their portfolio, and interact with their assets. Our stack is React on web and React Native on mobile, and we ship fast, measure everything, and iterate based on real user behaviour. We work agile, globally distributed, and we care as much about why we build something as how we build it. We're looking for a world-class Senior Frontend Engineer to join our product-minded engineering team: we care about customer problems, measurable outcomes, frontend craft, and fast iteration. We work across web and mobile surfaces, partner closely with Product, Design, Data, and Platform teams, and use experimentation, observability, and user behaviour to guide what we build next. THE OPPORTUNITY - Design, develop, and maintain high-quality consumer-facing features across web (React) and mobile (React Native), owning the full experience from concept to production monitoring. - Own the full lifecycle of product work, from discovery and technical design through release, monitoring, experimentation, and iteration. - Drive A/B testing and experimentation strategies forming hypotheses, designing experiments, analysing results, and iterating based on data. - Partner with Product, Design, Data, and Mobile engineers to create coherent experiences across Kraken’s consumer surfaces. - Make opinionated technical decisions on framework and architecture choices (we want engineers who have strong views on things like TanStack Router vs Next.js App Router and can back them up with real experience). - Set the standard for high-quality code — functional correctness, accessibility, performance, and testability are non-negotiables. - Mentor engineers across seniority levels and contribute to a culture of craft and continuous improvement. - Lead and collaborate on complex cross-platform initiatives, driving alignment across web and mobile surfaces. - Stay ahead of the curve on React ecosystem tooling, React Server Components, concurrent features, streaming, and bring those insights back to the team. - Work AI-natively, we use AI tools across the full SDLC and expect engineers to have a structured, opinionated workflow, not just autocomplete. WHAT YOU BRING - 6+ years of professional software development experience with a strong focus on consumer-facing web and/or mobile products. - Deep expertise in TypeScript and the React ecosystem, you have opinions about state management, data fetching patterns, and component architecture, and you can articulate the trade-offs. - Production experience with React Native and cross-platform mobile development, including App Store and Google Play release pipelines. - Experience with Next.js — specifically familiarity with App Router, React Server Components, and the client/server boundary decisions that come with them. - Hands-on experience with A/B testing, feature flags, and experimentation frameworks (LaunchDarkly, Optimizely, or similar). - Experience with WebSockets or Server-Sent Events for real-time UI updates. - Strong testing culture Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright or Cypress, and the judgement to know when to use each. - Familiarity with modern build tooling (Vite, Webpack, CI/CD pipelines) and performance profiling. - Experience in fintech, crypto, payments, or other high-trust consumer products where correctness and user confidence matter. - Strong written and verbal English, you can write a clear RFC, give direct feedback in a PR review, and explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical stakeholder. - An active AI-assisted development workflow, Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, or equivalent with the engineering rigour to review and own what gets produced. Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. items.title: Head of Fraud
items.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and trust in every account, deposit and trade is core to the product. As Head of Fraud, you will own Polymarket's fraud risk end to end: defining the strategy, building preventative and detective controls, and making sure every finding is resolved. Your scope covers first-party fraud (customers abusing the platform themselves) and third-party fraud (bad actors targeting our users and systems, including account takeover). You will hold the bar for what good looks like both commercially and in the eyes of our regulators, and you will move fast. You will partner with and influence Product owners and engineers you don't manage build and ship most fraud controls, so influencing them is critical to success in this role. You'll also work closely with Compliance, Legal, Data, Payments, Customer Support and Security. WHAT YOU'LL OWN Strategy and risk ownership - Own the fraud risk framework and appetite, and set the roadmap to deliver it. - Maintain a living fraud risk assessment and typology library across onboarding, funding, trading and withdrawals. - Report fraud exposure, losses, control performance and emerging threats to senior leadership and governance forums. Preventative and detective controls - Partner with Product and Engineering to assess fraud risk before new products, payment methods, promotions, and material feature changes launch. - Define and implement controls that stop fraud before it happens: identity and device signals, step-up authentication, velocity and limit rules, and payment and withdrawal checks. - Build detective controls that surface fraud fast: monitoring rules, ML and AI models, anomaly detection, alerting and case management. - Tune controls continuously against loss rates, false positives and customer friction. Fraud types in scope - First-party fraud: chargeback and friendly fraud, promotion and referral abuse, ACH fraud, multi-accounting, and identity misrepresentation by genuine customers. - Third-party fraud: account takeover, synthetic and stolen identities, stolen payment methods, phishing, social engineering, scams, and organized fraud rings. Findings and resolution - Own investigations, from triage to root cause to closure. - Make sure every finding from monitoring, audits, regulatory exams and incidents has an owner, a fix and a deadline, and is closed out. - Feed lessons back into product, controls and policy so issues don't recur. Team and partnership - Build and lead a high-performing fraud team of analysts, investigators and fraud data specialists. - Drive delivery through Product and Engineering: shape their roadmaps, win prioritization for fraud work, and design prevention into features from day one. - Work with Compliance and Legal on regulatory expectations, SAR-related escalations and exam readiness. - Select and manage fraud vendors and tooling. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR Influence is the most critical skill for this role, and we'll assess it at every interview stage. - Exceptional influence. You have a track record of getting fraud controls shipped by product and engineering teams you don't manage. You build trust fast, make a clear case using data, win prioritization against competing roadmaps, and turn disagreement into decisions. - Deep fraud expertise. 10+ years of experience in fraud within fintech, payments, banking, crypto, trading, online gaming, or other high-volume digital platforms, including at least five years in leadership, with direct accountability for fraud prevention, investigations, operations, and measurable outcomes. - Control design that works. A track record of building preventative and detective controls from scratch and proving they cut losses without hurting good customers. - Breadth across fraud types. Hands-on experience with both first-party and third-party fraud, including account takeover, identity fraud and payment fraud. - AI native. You use AI and automation as your default way of working: for detection models, investigation tooling, case triage and your own day-to-day productivity. You know where models beat rules and where they don't. - Commercial judgement. You understand that the goal is the right balance of loss, friction and growth, not zero fraud. You can put a number on the trade-offs. - Regulatory lens. You know what regulators expect from a fraud program (governance, documentation, testing, escalation) and can defend our approach in an exam. - Pace and ownership. You drive outcomes quickly, prioritize ruthlessly and close things out. You're comfortable in a fast-moving, high-growth environment. - Data fluency. Comfortable working directly in SQL and with data teams to size problems and measure control performance. NICE TO HAVE - Experience at a regulated exchange, derivatives venue or broker, or at a crypto platform with on-chain and fiat flows. - Familiarity with blockchain analytics and wallet-level risk signals. - Exposure to market abuse and trade surveillance, and how it intersects with fraud. - Experience building fraud capability across multiple jurisdictions. - Hands-on experience shipping LLM or agent-based tooling for investigations. BENEFITS - Competitive salary & equity - Unlimited PTO - Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage - 401k match - Hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, big display, & accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $500,000 to $600,000 plus equity and benefits. This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

items.title: People Tech & Analytics Engineer
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a People Tech & Analytics Engineer on the People team, you will build the systems, data pipelines, and automations behind how Mistral runs People Operations. Reporting to the People Tech & Analytics Lead, you will turn the roadmap into reality: wiring our HR tech stack together, making data flow reliably between systems, and automating people processes with third-party tools as well as Mistral's own models, agents, and APIs. This is an individual contributor role for someone who loves building. You will spend most of your time in the systems and the data, deep-diving into problems: connecting HRIS, ATS, payroll, identity, and finance tools, standing up the data layer behind our people metrics, and shipping automations that remove manual work from the People team. If you are a data engineer or people technology specialist who wants to deliver meaningful automation outcomes at Europe's largest AI company, this is the role for you. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Build, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations and data pipelines across our HR systems (HRIS, ATS, payroll, identity and finance), run data quality checks, and fix inconsistencies at the source. - Implement and evolve the Metabase visualisation layer of our people data lake, build the dashboards and self-serve reporting managers and People partners rely on, as well as the context layer on HR data, supporting the move to conversational insights in collaboration with the Data team. - Design, build, test and document automated workflows, mainly with Mistral's own models, agents and APIs, with human review wherever decisions affect people, monitor live automations with alerting, error handling, logging and runbooks, and prototype AI use cases on people processes, productionising the ones that prove their worth. - Implement configuration changes across the HR tech stack (workflows, fields, roles and permissions, new countries and entities), support testing and rollout of system changes and integrations, and act as first-line troubleshooter for the People team, leading issue resolution through to production with a clear audit trail. - Architect end-to-end HR workflows with key stakeholders in HR Operations, Business Partnering and Reward, and implement data governance in practice: quality standards, access controls, retention rules and audit trails for employee data. - Provide clear enablement materials in Notion so the People team and managers can use our systems confidently, with strong tier-1 support via a bot. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Experience in analytics engineering or HR technology, ideally within an HR or People function or working closely with one as a stakeholder. - Strong practical SQL: you are comfortable building pipelines and transformations yourself. - Hands-on experience with HR systems such as Ashby, and integrating them with ATS, payroll, identity and finance tools via APIs, middleware and data pipelines. - Real automation experience: you have built and maintained workflows in n8n or similar tools such as Make, Zapier, Workato or Langdock, and you are excited to do the same with Mistral's own models and tooling. - Working experience with data warehousing (Snowflake, BigQuery) and the modern data stack (dbt or similar), and with visualisation tools such as Metabase, Looker, Tableau or Power BI. - You are low-ego and team-spirited, and you take a prioritised problem and run with it in ambiguity: you would rather build a first version and iterate than wait for a perfect spec. You start from the HR need, not the technology, stay hands-on, and have a track record of building foundations in growing organisations without creating legacy. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. items.title: Commercial Counsel - Brazil
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an experienced Commercial Counsel to join our Legal Team in Brazil. In this role, you will support complex commercial transactions with a primary focus on Brazil and support for other LATAM countries, including SaaS, licensing, and strategic partnerships, while helping the company navigate diverse legal and regulatory frameworks in the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence. items.description: We’re looking for an Lead Data Engineer to join the Paid Media Insights team within Better Collective. The Domanin Paid media is where the data has to pay off. We spend real money across dozens of ad networks every day. Which campaigns scale, which creatives get cut and which markets get budget comes out of this team’s models. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, stitched into one user-level view of what a click was worth. That model exists and it works. The most demanding domain on our platform: the most sources, the fastest schema churn, the shortest patience for a late table. We want the engineer who owns it. Where this role sits A central platform team sets the how. You set the what. A central team owns the platform - MotherDuck, dbt, Dagster, DLT, the infrastructure. Paid Media Insights is a spoke in that hub and spoke organisation, building on it. The split is deliberate: the platform team decides how data is produced, you decide what paid media produces and own everything we run. No new stack to build, and no year lost to plumbing a central team should solve once. Be a demanding customer: when a golden path does not fit paid media, push for it to change rather than quietly building around it. You report to the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights and work across Paid Media, with the Campaign, Commercial, CRM and platform teams. What you will own Every data job in paid media. All of it. Freshness, cost, reliability, alerting, and the 07:30 incident before the spend review. A paid media model that is wrong or late is yours, not the platform team’s - that accountability is the core of the role. The end-to-end user-level model. Ad platform spend and delivery, affiliate and operator revenue and CRM, joined into one view the business trusts enough to move budget on. Ingestion of paid media sources on the platform’s framework: which sources, which schemas, and what happens when a network changes its API unannounced. The domain’s models, from staging to the marts analysts query, plus the semantic meaning on top. Nobody at the centre can define a qualified signup in paid media. You can. Reverse ETL into the ad platforms, so conversion data lands where it changes bidding. The handover, taking over the paid media jobs the central team still runs for us. What you will lead A group of engineers, and the standard they build to Technical lead for the data engineers in Paid Media Insights: setting the standard for how this domain builds, reviewing, unblocking, and growing them by giving away the interesting problems. Shaping the domain’s roadmap with the Senior Head of Paid Media Insights, the analysts and the business teams. Representing paid media in platform conversations, including how we support machine learning and data science. Hands-on technical leadership, not a step away from building. You will be in the code. What we’re looking for More than a stack match, we are looking for a particular way of working. You take ownership, and it shows up in the boring parts. You want the pager as well as the model, and would rather own a domain end to end than hand off the consequences. You break complex systems into simple parts. Attribution windows, late conversions, identity across platforms, dozens of disagreeing source APIs - you hold that and still hand the business something it can reason about. You raise the people around you. Colleagues come to you for technical advice. You review generously, give feedback that lands, and would rather the whole team understand the pipeline than be the only one who does. You work well with a platform team. Strong opinions about standards, still happy to work inside someone else’s. You know a constraint worth fighting from a preference worth dropping. You are already past prompting. AI is part of how you engineer, and you have a view on what a data domain needs to be for agents to be useful on top of it: documented, standardised, semantically clear. You are close to the business. You will sit with the marketers and analysts spending budget on what you build, and can talk data with people who do not think in tables. You are technically deep where it counts. Production pipelines in SQL and Python, dbt and Dagster, cloud data warehousing, and a real feel for performance, cost and reliability at scale. Paid media or attribution experience is a bonus. Our Stack What you will build on MotherDuck / DuckDB · dbt · Dagster · DLT · Python · SQL · AWS · reverse ETL and semantic layer tooling We do not expect you to have worked with all of these. If you have built production pipelines on Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift and you are curious about where we are going, that transfers. items.title: Data Science Tech Lead Manager, Model Experience
items.location_text: New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company's mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world. You'll be the senior data science leader for Model Experience and a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders. Working where frontier AI research reaches the public, you'll help shape model roadmap and launch decisions, bringing a point of view on how users experience our models and what good looks like beyond benchmark scores. As a tech lead manager, you'll also hire and manage a team of data scientists, setting their agenda, personally leading the highest-stakes analyses, and raising the bar for how data shapes model and product decisions. Responsibilities: Act as a strategic thought partner to product, engineering, and research leaders, helping shape model roadmap priorities, launch decisions, and the major bets the team makes Set the data science agenda for Model Experience, deciding where the team can have the most impact on model development and launch decisions and what it should deprioritize Hire, manage, and develop a team of data scientists, coaching them to move from answering questions to shaping decisions Frame the most important and ambiguous questions about model quality and user experience, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction Define how Model Experience measures success, establishing the core metrics and measurement frameworks across external products and internal testing that align teams and leadership on what matters Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Model Experience, including where launches lack a clean A/B test, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses Turn complex analyses of model and user behavior into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Model Experience needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our models and products evolve You may be a good fit if you: Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a product or research area at significant scale Have 3+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction, hiring, and developing senior data scientists Have been a trusted partner to senior product, research, and business leaders, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision Bring strong product sense and business judgment, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others' technical work Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress Care about the company's mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI Strong candidates may also have: Experience with AI/ML products, large language models, or developer tools in the AI/ML ecosystem Experience as a tech lead manager or player-coach, balancing hands-on technical work with people management Experience building or scaling a data science team in a fast-growing organization Experience working closely with Product or Research teams, especially on LLM or AI products Comfort working with unstructured data The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $380,000 — $460,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: About the Team OpenAI's data center construction teams work with engineering, supply chain, safety, quality, commissioning and operations partners to deliver the infrastructure that supports our computing needs. Mechanical delivery brings together cooling equipment, plant, piping and controls interfaces so that systems are installed, tested and ready for commissioning. About the Role As a Mechanical Lead, you will lead mechanical field delivery for data center construction, including cooling infrastructure, mechanical yards, piping and data hall fit-out. You will oversee general contractors, specialist installers and service providers, combining practical mechanical expertise with hands-on field leadership. Your focus will be safe installation, contractor performance, coordinated interfaces and complete evidence for commissioning and operational handover. Key Responsibilities - Manage mechanical contractors, equipment and piping installers, and general-contractor interfaces against approved scope, schedule and quality requirements. - Oversee installation readiness and delivery of cooling plant, pumps, heat rejection equipment, air handling, piping and applicable liquid-cooling infrastructure. - Coordinate equipment placement, pipe routing, supports, access and maintainability with structural, electrical, controls and hardware teams. - Review contractor work plans, constructability, submittals, RFIs and change proposals; resolve field issues with the responsible engineering teams. - Oversee pressure testing, flushing, cleaning and inspection records; verify completion, defect closure and commissioning readiness. - Support commissioning specialists with mechanical startup and system tests, corrective work and complete as-built, operating and maintenance documentation. - Set contractor priorities, review staffing and progress, identify constraints early and coordinate recovery actions with construction leadership. - Maintain clear progress, risk and change reporting, with accountable handoffs between construction partners and OpenAI teams. items.description: About the Team OpenAI's Industrial Compute organization delivers the infrastructure that powers frontier AI models. Within Infrastructure Delivery, we turn engineering concepts into safe, reliable, and operational AI campuses by working across design, construction, utilities, commissioning, operations, and external partners. The fire protection function establishes the life-safety and property-protection strategy for these campuses. The team connects code requirements and engineering standards to practical design, construction, testing, incident readiness, and long-term operations. About the Role We are seeking a Fire Protection Engineer to lead owner-side fire and life-safety engineering across large-scale data center programs. You will establish design criteria, review complex fire protection systems, coordinate with authorities and delivery partners, and ensure that fire and life-safety requirements remain clear from early design through construction, commissioning, and operational handover. This role requires strong technical judgment across detection, alarm, suppression, smoke control, water supply, emergency response, and code compliance. You will work closely with engineering, construction, safety, security, commissioning, and operations teams to resolve risks quickly without compromising life safety, reliability, or schedule. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain fire protection and life-safety design criteria, technical standards, and review requirements for self-build data center campuses. - Review fire protection drawings, specifications, code analyses, fire and life-safety narratives, hydraulic calculations, equipment submittals, and sequences of operation across all project phases. - Provide owner-side engineering direction for fire detection and alarm, automatic suppression, fire pumps and water storage, smoke control, emergency communication, and related life-safety systems. - Integrate fire protection requirements with architectural, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, security, hardware, and operational systems. - Partner with code officials, authorities having jurisdiction, insurers, consultants, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve code interpretations and approval risks. - Support constructability reviews, RFIs, submittals, field inspections, deficiency resolution, and change management during active construction. - Define commissioning, integrated-system testing, acceptance, turnover, and operational-readiness criteria for fire and life-safety systems. - Assess fire and life-safety risks associated with high-density compute, battery and energy-storage systems, generators and fuel systems, utility infrastructure, cooling systems, hazardous materials, and construction activities. - Support incident response, root-cause reviews, corrective actions, and lessons learned, translating operational findings into improved designs and standards. - Maintain clear records of design decisions, code positions, approvals, testing results, open risks, and turnover requirements. - Travel regularly to project sites to support design reviews, field execution, testing, commissioning, and operational readiness. items.location_text: San Francisco, Remote (United States), Seattle, New York City
items.description: Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast. RESPONSIBILITIES - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost. - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load. - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers. - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested. - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back. - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works. - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice. - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure. - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team. QUALIFICATIONS We expect you to have real depth in most of these: - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them. - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count. - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down. - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing). - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it. - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter. - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes. - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you. ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets. - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF. - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar. - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls. - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch. - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar). - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

Creators stream on KICK across gaming, talk shows, podcasts, IRL, sport and events. Other perks 18 weeks of paid parental leave for primary carers, so you can be there for the moments that matter. Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage. Matched 401(k) contributions, so your future grows alongside your career. We play fair. We hire fair. True to our value of ‘Play fair’ we always hire fair. Our work and our brands are fuelled by our diverse culture. We hire for talent and grit. But we never discriminate. Your race, religion, nationality, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital, veteran, or disability status won’t affect our hiring decision, or your trajectory here. items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Financial Crimes (FinCrimes) Sanctions team plays a critical role in protecting Robinhood and its customers by identifying, investigating, and mitigating sanctions-related risks across our products and global operations. The team supports a rapidly evolving business, including cryptocurrency, brokerage, and money movement activities, while maintaining compliance with applicable U.S. and international sanctions requirements. As a Sanctions Crypto Investigator you will be responsible for investigating potential sanctions exposure associated with cryptocurrency transactions, digital asset wallets, and customer activity. You will leverage blockchain analytics, investigative tools, and sound risk-based judgment to identify potential sanctions violations, assess complex transaction activity, and document defensible investigative conclusions. This role is based in our Denver, CO, Westlake, TX, or New York NY office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Conduct thorough investigations of cryptocurrency-related sanctions alerts, including customer screening matches, deposits, withdrawals, wallet addresses, and blockchain transactions. Leverage blockchain analytics tools, including TRM Labs or similar platforms, to evaluate direct and indirect sanctions exposure, trace transaction activity, and identify potential sanctions evasion typologies. Review and disposition potential matches against OFAC and other applicable sanctions lists, ensuring timely, accurate, and well-documented investigative decisions. Identify and escalate potential sanctions violations, including transactions or assets that may require blocking, rejecting, or additional regulatory review. Prepare clear, concise, and comprehensive investigative narratives, supporting documentation, and escalation recommendations. Monitor emerging cryptocurrency sanctions risks, regulatory developments, and illicit finance typologies to support ongoing risk identification and mitigation. Partner with Compliance, Legal, Engineering, Product, and other FinCrimes teams to resolve complex investigations and enhance sanctions screening capabilities. Identify opportunities to improve investigative workflows, screening effectiveness, operational efficiency, and automation. Assist with regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, quality assurance reviews, and management reporting. Maintain adherence to established procedures, regulatory requirements, and internal service-level expectations while managing investigative workloads. What you bring 3+ years of experience in financial crimes, sanctions investigations, AML compliance, or a related field within financial services, fintech, cryptocurrency, or another regulated environment. Demonstrated experience investigating cryptocurrency transactions and assessing financial crimes or sanctions-related risks. Working knowledge of blockchain technology, digital asset transactions, wallet addresses, and cryptocurrency transaction flows. Experience using blockchain analytics tools such as TRM Labs, Chainalysis, Elliptic, or comparable platforms. Strong understanding of OFAC sanctions regulations, sanctions screening requirements, and common sanctions evasion methodologies. Experience conducting complex investigations, evaluating potential true positive matches, and preparing clear, defensible investigative documentation. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to assess complex information and make sound, risk-based decisions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate investigative findings and recommendations effectively. Ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain a high degree of accuracy in a fast-paced environment. A collaborative mindset and willingness to partner across teams to solve problems and improve existing processes. High standards of integrity, professionalism, and discretion when handling confidential or sensitive information. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill. items.description: Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US. We're building a more proactive data function, and this role is its deep-investigation engine. Your findings will inform experiments, the roadmap and company strategy. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Go looking for what nobody asked about. This is the heart of the role. You'll notice when something looks off in a funnel, a cohort or a metric, disappear into it, and come back with a product issue, a cost leak or an opportunity nobody was looking for. You set much of your own agenda, and you don't wait for a request to start digging. - Lead deep investigations into user behaviour and customer experience across product and non-product touchpoints, including support, customer success and sales. - Find where activation breaks. Identify failure points in the user journey, including those that could become productised capabilities. - Understand acquisition and intent. Dig into acquisition channels, user use cases and what people are actually trying to achieve. - Do rigorous causal and statistical work. Go beyond correlation with regression, causal analysis and well-designed experiments, and be clear about what the evidence does and doesn't support. - Build models that drive action. Apply data science to real business problems, such as churn modelling that can trigger real-time product action, and explain clearly how models are applied and what impact they have. - Analyse unstructured and AI-specific data. Work with agent-user conversations, context layers and evaluation systems alongside structured product data. - Size opportunities. Produce market opportunity sizing that helps the business prioritise. - Measure how we build. Partner with engineering managers on organisational productivity metrics. - Communicate for impact. Translate findings into clear recommendations for product teams, management and executives. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR MUST-HAVES - Deep product analytics experience across growth and broader product areas, with a record of investigations that changed decisions. - Data science and modelling experience, and the ability to explain how you applied it and what business impact it had. - Strong grounding in correlation, regression and causal analysis. - A proactive approach. You surface insights and shape the agenda rather than working to a brief. - Genuine curiosity. You notice what looks off and dig until you understand why. - Clear communication with management and executives about business impact, simplifying complex analysis into actionable recommendations. PREFERRED - Experience with unstructured data. - Experience at an AI-native company, or with the added data complexity AI products bring. - Understanding of subscription businesses. - Understanding of the PLG motions in a B2B space. BONUS POINTS IF YOU'VE… - Worked on multi-product platforms where upsells, cross-sells and bundling were a key revenue driver. - Worked alongside qualitative research, connecting the what (data) with the why (qual). - Done pricing and packaging work: willingness-to-pay, price testing, bundle performance. - HOW WE WORK We optimise for responsibility and freedom. - No ticket conveyor belt. We run on ownership and a small number of high-impact projects. - Close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Growth and commercial teams to ship real outcomes. - A bias toward pragmatic solutions that get used, measured and improved. WHY JOIN - Do the hardest, most interesting analytical work in the company, with direct line of sight to product and strategy decisions. - Work across structured and unstructured data, customer conversations and AI evaluation, at the intersection of product usage, AI and revenue. - Independence and impact at principal level, without the management overhead.
